When chasing "is the console clean?" or "what error did the user see?", three
durable, NON-overlapping surfaces exist. Query ALL THREE and reconcile — any one
alone is a false "clean" signal.

## 1. `toastLog` (server-side, PG) — user-facing toasts

Every `toast.error()` / `addToast()` call. Pull via:

```sh
curl -sS "http://localhost:3055/api/zero-harness/rest-query?name=toastLog.recent&args=%7B%22limit%22%3A100%7D" \
  | jq -r '.rows[] | "\(.createdAt | tonumber / 1000 | strftime("%H:%M:%S")) [\(.level)] \(.message)"'
```

Schema: `{id, level, message, description, harnessSlug, createdAt, actionLabel, actionHref}` (timestamps UTC).

**Use this first** for "what errors did the user see?". `tauri-agent-tools
console-monitor --duration N` only captures logs fired DURING its N-second window —
anything from page load, a prior session, or earlier in the same session is invisible;
the persistent toastLog has all of it. Query patterns: last N errors
`.rows[] | select(.level == "error")`; distinct
`.rows[].message | sed 's/[0-9]\+/N/g' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn`; since-ts filter
on `createdAt > <ms>`.

## 2. `window.__papercuspPerfRecorder.events` (client-side, localStorage) — JS errors

`apps/operator/app/admin/testing/_lib/vitals-recorder.ts` patches `console.error` +
`window.error` + `unhandledrejection` → `localStorage['papercusp.testing.perf-events.v1']`.

**Scope caveat:** `PerfObserverProvider` (which calls `startRecorder()`) only mounts on
`/admin/testing` pages. On every other route `window.__papercuspPerfRecorder` is
`undefined` and `events.length` returns 0 vacuously — **NOT a valid "clean" signal for
`/setup`, `/harness`, `/marketplace`, etc.** For those routes use
`tauri-agent-tools capture -o <dir>` and read `<dir>/console-errors.json` (taps WebKit's
devtools console directly). It catches what never writes a toast:

- React errors ("Rendered more hooks…", hydration errors)
- `ChunkLoadError`, module/compile errors (Turbopack/SWC parse failures)
- Unhandled promise rejections

Query via `tauri-agent-tools eval`:

```js
JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('papercusp.testing.perf-events.v1') || '[]')
  .filter(e => e.kind === 'console-error' || e.kind === 'unhandled-error')
```

Group by `e.detail.slice(0, 80)` to collapse repeats. **Clearing it:** the recorder keeps
an in-memory `events` array AND flushes to localStorage, so `localStorage.removeItem`
alone is undone by the next flush — reset both:

```js
if (window.__papercuspPerfRecorder) window.__papercuspPerfRecorder.events = [];
localStorage.removeItem('papercusp.testing.perf-events.v1');
location.reload();
```

## 3. `tauri-agent-tools console-monitor` (live bridge stream) — WebKit's direct logs

WebKit logs some errors **directly to the devtools console without going through
`console.error`** — invisible to BOTH surfaces above:

- `Fetch API cannot load X due to access control checks` (often a *timeout*, not CORS)
- `Load failed` on fetches WebKit aborted before resolution
- Network-layer warnings (mixed content, certificate, …)

```sh
tauri-agent-tools console-monitor --port <port> --token <tok> --duration 30000 --json --level error > /tmp/cm.json
```

…and reload the page during the window — the bridge taps the webview's ENTIRE console feed.

**⚠ `"Fetch API cannot load X due to access control checks"` is misleading — on WebKitGTK
it almost always means the fetch TIMED OUT (Next dev lazy-compile slowness), not real
CORS.** Check `curl -w "%{time_total}"` against the same URL before chasing ACAO headers;
the fix is to pre-warm the slow route before the webview fetches it (first-hit dev
compile latency), not to chase ACAO headers.

## Trichotomy summary

| Surface | Catches | Misses |
|---|---|---|
| `toastLog.recent` | `toast.error()` / `addToast()` | everything else |
| `__papercuspPerfRecorder` | JS `console.error` / `window.error` / rejections (only on `/admin/testing`) | WebKit's direct devtools logs |
| `console-monitor` (bridge) | the entire webview console feed | anything before its start window |

For "is the console clean now?", query **all three** and reconcile.
